title: Deployment Strategies
description: Master blue-green, canary, traffic shifting, feature flags at scale with LaunchDarkly architecture, and progressive delivery pipelines.

segments.text: Deploying to production is the riskiest moment in the software lifecycle. A bad deploy at Knight Capital cost them four hundred forty million dollars in forty-five minutes. Deployment strategies manage this risk by controlling how new code reaches users. The goal: if something goes wrong, limit the blast radius and roll back instantly.

Blue-green deployment: maintain two identical environments. Blue runs the current version. Deploy the new version to green. Test green thoroughly. Switch the load balancer from blue to green. If green fails, switch back to blue instantly — rollback is one DNS change or load balancer flip. The downside: you need double the infrastructure.

Canary deployment: route a small percentage of traffic to the new version — start with one percent. Monitor error rates, latency, and business metrics. If healthy, increase to five, ten, twenty-five, fifty, one hundred percent over hours or days. Google deploys to one canary cluster first, monitors for twenty-four hours, then rolls out globally.

Traffic shifting with weighted routing gives fine-grained control. Istio VirtualService: ninety-five percent to v1, five percent to v2. Increment v2 weight based on automated health checks. AWS App Mesh and Linkerd provide similar traffic splitting. The routing happens at the proxy layer — no application code changes needed.

Your canary at five percent traffic shows p99 latency increased from two hundred to three hundred milliseconds. Error rate is unchanged. Is this a problem? What's your decision framework for proceeding, pausing, or rolling back?
segments.thought_prompt: Canary shows 50% p99 latency increase but no error rate change. Proceed, pause, or rollback?

segments.text: Feature flags decouple deployment from release. Deploy code to production with the feature disabled. Enable for internal users first, then beta users, then one percent of all users, then everyone. LaunchDarkly evaluates flags in under ten milliseconds using a local SDK cache synced via streaming connection. Netflix manages over five thousand concurrent feature flags.

LaunchDarkly's architecture: SDKs in every service maintain a local flag store. A streaming connection pushes flag changes in real-time — sub-hundred-millisecond propagation. No network call per flag evaluation — all evaluations are local. The relay proxy handles high-throughput environments. Flag evaluations happen at over one hundred thousand evaluations per second per server.

Progressive delivery combines canary deployments with automated analysis. Argo Rollouts and Flagger monitor canary metrics, automatically promote or rollback based on predefined success criteria. Define: error rate less than one percent AND p99 latency less than five hundred milliseconds AND no increase in five-hundred errors. Full automation from deploy to one hundred percent traffic.

Database migrations are the hardest deployment problem. You can't blue-green a database. Use expand-and-contract: add the new column, deploy code that writes to both old and new columns, backfill existing data, deploy code that reads from the new column, drop the old column. Each step is independently deployable and rollbackable.

Design the deployment pipeline for a microservices platform with one hundred services, each deploying ten times per day. Include canary analysis, feature flags, database migrations, and rollback procedures.
segments.thought_prompt: Design deployment for 100 services deploying 10x/day: canary, flags, DB migrations, rollback.

segments.text: Deployment strategies form a spectrum from simple to sophisticated: blue-green for instant rollback, canary for gradual validation, feature flags for decoupling deploy from release, and progressive delivery for full automation. The Staff-level practice: every deployment should be reversible within minutes, and database migrations should follow the expand-and-contract pattern.
